name: i write with a blush
content: Not long ago there was a man. We were a hundred feet above ground—something like that—and he was smoking crack. The platform was baren of souls; it was just him, I, and this prick security officer walking towards us from the far end. Neither of us were in a hurry for the train. Nevertheless it raced Mister Prick and got to us before he could and whisked us away.

I was nervous on Crack Man’s behalf, I will not lie. He did not seem to be very bothered by the situation at all, which actually is rather quintessential of him. When you enter the sliding doors of the train—subway, metro, lightrail, yada—to your left are two short rising steps, and on this raised platform there are four rows of seats, each with two on either side of an aisle. You turn left of the doors, now facing the end of the aisle, and climb onto the raised platform. I want you to imagine this. Number the rows one (frontmost, closest to the door) to four (farthest back), and seat positions A (looking toward the door, leftmost) to D (looking…door, rightmost). On four D sat this man, and on two B, I. In all fairness, I didn’t choose to sit here: to be mesmerized is not much of a choice but rather a very welcome inconvenience. Harrowed as I may be, though, I am a good boy and so I listened to one C and shut up and did not question a thing—though one very well could’ve seen her and turned right of the doors instead. Recall that I say one, for one is not I.

Crack Man needs my attention. As much as I’d like not to, I defy the laws of Bollywood and leave my seat, and the view. One C glances? Or doesn’t? I’m not sure. She did glance at some point but I was too busy to recall when exactly; I am selfish and therefore instead of on her I was focusing on not getting stabbed. I figured that if I didn’t talk to Crack Man he would stab me. I met him first at the station, remember? This motherfucker knew me as Comrade, and my defection would’ve been sacrilegious. I listened. He spoke to me and I listened to him. It was gibberish for the most part—bullshit—until this crackhead decided to get serious. He said something terrible happened in Israel sometime in October of last year; I queried if he meant October 7th, 2024, and he did. In response to this I abandoned my seat and stood in the aisle and bent to his side, my ear next to his crack-mouth. I told him, in secret, that for a short moment in my life I was in a Hebrew acapella group. This was not a lie: I served Tenor II in the Chai Notes, and I sang their repertoire and performed at a concert, and I received gifts from their mums, and I hugged them with intent and with meaning. At this point I felt it was most appropriate to fuck off rather than wait for his response. I don’t know what sort of white he was.

She’s still in one C—no—one C is still hers. I cannot focus on this, obviously, because Mister Crack is still talking to me—rather, at me. I shift my body and turn my neck on a one-fifty-degree radial (assuming that forward is North) and glance back. By this time he’s very fervently inquiring about my religion, and whether or not I believe that there is one God™. One C glances, and this I’m confident of; I think she likes my guts. She glanced, to be fair to her, before Crack Man started listing the religions of the world hoping I’d indicate my preference; her not glancing at this time was sort of like choosing to not look at someone’s password while they type it—very polite, we love that in this house.

Finally his schizophrenia kicks in and he begins talking to the guy sitting next to him (with unfettered enthusiasm). I do feel bad for them both. Now I get to work. This entire time I’ve had in my hands a little pink pad of sticky notes and my trusty UniBall. Take one. I write out my number but I don’t like the way I made the second 7. Scratch that; a single swipe rips it off and crushes it. Take two. I write my name in cursive but the Y is a bit too flamboyant; rip two. Take three. I add an innocuous :) at the end for good measure. I don’t fold—that is for her to do.
Crack Man departs his abode. He stumbles past her and his instability brushes her left arm and I’m fucking appalled. I mouth a “sorry” on this asshat’s behalf.
By now we’ve moled our way back into the ground. All we see as light is filament in white. Time, in my head, pauses here for what feels like forever. And then her station shows up.
She walks down the aisle, whatever of it remains. Down one step, then another. Doors slide open to either side and I fly out of my seat.
“You dropped something”, and I hand her the note. Before she’s gone she smiles and that is enough.
Doors close, I begin to blush, we move onto the next station. As of yet this beginning has been interminable.
All is an interminable chain of longing.
